newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens revises sales, orders outlook up.
newsitem.headline: Siemens revises sales, orders outlook up.

text.p: German electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG has revised upward its outlook for sales and incoming orders, chairman Heinrich von Pierer said on Thursday.
In the text of remarks prepared for delivery at the company's annual general meeting, von Pierer repeated his forecast of stable earnings in 1996/97, with a rise again in 1997/98.
Siemens revises sales, orders outlook up
"We expect a rise in incoming orders and sales above that in our initial, rather subdued plans," von Pierer said.
A favourable foreign exchange market and low interest rates have boosted the outlook, he said.

Von Pierer said profit in the current business year, which began on October 1, will be stable at last year's 2.5 billion marks, without extraordinary items. It will then rise again next year, he said.
Siemens aims to improve its position in world markets and its profitability by spinning off dead-end businesses, acquiring others with better prospects, and expanding in new fields, he said.
